question: What is another name commonly used for leprosy?
explanation: Leprosy is also called Hansen's disease, named after the scientist who discovered the causative bacterium. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which parts of the body are mainly affected by leprosy?
explanation: The leprosy bacteria love cooler areas of the body, which is why they mainly attack the skin and the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the name of the bacterium that causes leprosy?
explanation: Mycobacterium leprae is the specific acid-fast bacillus responsible for causing leprosy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why is it often hard to tell exactly when someone caught leprosy?

options.A: It takes a very long time for signs to show up
options.B: Early symptoms always go away on their own
options.C: It spreads through dirty drinking water
options.D: The bacteria die instantly outside the body

explanation: Because symptoms can take months or even years to appear, it is tough to trace back the exact moment of exposure. Don't worry, you're learning! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the highest number of skin patches a patient can have to be classified as having paucibacillary leprosy?
explanation: Paucibacillary simply means 'few bacteria.' Clinically, it's marked by having between one and five skin patches. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h3)

question: What main factor decides if a patient develops mild (paucibacillary) or severe (multibacillary) leprosy?

options.D: The strength of the patient's immune system

explanation: It all comes down to how well the body's immune system fights off the bacteria. A stronger defense means fewer lesions! You're getting the hang of this. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is usually the very first sign of leprosy on the skin?

options.A: A discolored patch that feels numb or less sensitive
options.B: Tiny water blisters on the hands
options.C: Painful open sores on the legs
options.D: Severe itching all over the body

explanation: A pale or reddish skin patch that doesn't feel normal touch or temperature is the classic early warning sign. Keep shining! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h4)

question: A patient comes in with a swollen ulnar nerve and a numb patch on the arm. What should you suspect?
explanation: When a nerve is thickened and a skin patch loses its feeling, leprosy should immediately come to mind. Spotting these clues makes you a great nurse! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do leprosy patients often end up with serious sores on their hands and feet?

options.A: Unbearable itching makes them scratch too hard
options.B: Blood completely stops flowing to the fingers and toes
options.C: Loss of feeling causes them to injure themselves without knowing
options.D: Bacteria directly dissolve the skin cells

explanation: Because they can't feel pain, heat, or sharp objects, minor cuts go unnoticed and turn into nasty ulcers. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which facial nerve problem puts a leprosy patient at risk of going blind?
explanation: Lagophthalmos means the patient can't close their eyes fully. This leaves the eyeball dry and prone to damage. You're mastering clinical terms step by step! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is leprosy treated with a mix of different drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To cut out the need for blood tests
options.C: To stop the bacteria from becoming resistant to the drugs
options.D: To make the treatment cheaper to buy

explanation: Using a combination of medications ensures the smart little germs can't mutate and outsmart a single drug. Brilliant concept to know! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h6)

question: How long is the standard course of multi-drug therapy for a patient with multibacillary leprosy?
explanation: Multibacillary cases require a longer treatment duration, usually lasting 12 to 24 months, to clear the higher bacterial load. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is a very important self-care habit to teach a patient who cannot feel their feet?

options.A: Washing with harsh antiseptic spirit daily
options.B: Checking the feet every single day for cuts and sores
options.C: Walking barefoot to make the soles tougher
options.D: Soaking feet in hot water to boost blood flow

explanation: Since they won't feel pain from a thorn or scrape, daily mirror checks help catch injuries before they turn into bad ulcers. You are learning real patient care! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h7)

question: A recovering leprosy patient feels very depressed because people in the community are avoiding them. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise them to pack up and relocate to another state
options.B: Assure them that people will soon forget about it
options.C: Offer a listening ear and connect them with a support group
options.D: Tell the patient never to discuss their illness with anyone

explanation: Emotional support and connecting with others who understand are powerful ways to beat stigma and heal the mind. You're going to be a wonderfully empathetic nurse! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main public health step used to stop leprosy from spreading in a town or village?

options.A: Finding cases early and starting treatment right away
options.B: Washing living areas with heavy chemicals
options.C: Locking all infected people away in isolated camps
options.D: Giving mandatory vaccines to every newborn baby

explanation: Catching cases early and starting medications quickly stops the spread because treatment makes patients non-infectious! Public health in action! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h8)

question: Why do community health nurses keep a close eye on people living in the same house as a leprosy patient?

options.A: They are forced to pay for the patient's hospital bills
options.B: They are at higher risk because they spend so much time together
options.C: They are legally banned from leaving the house during treatment
options.D: They must swallow preventive antibiotics for years

explanation: Living closely under one roof means more exposure time, so checking family members regularly helps catch any early signs. Fantastic job completing this set! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h8)
